name: ubertooth
why: Open 2.4GHz sniffer that lets you follow Bluetooth LE traffic from your own desk; a real door into the radio air around you.

brief.what_it_is: Ubertooth is an open source 2.4 GHz wireless development platform aimed at Bluetooth experimentation, built around the Ubertooth One hardware board with a 2.4 GHz dipole antenna on an RP-SMA connector. Its main use is as a BLE (Bluetooth Smart) sniffer, and the README says it can also capture some data from Basic Rate Bluetooth Classic connections. The host-side tools (ubertooth-btle, ubertooth-btbr, ubertooth-rx, ubertooth-specan, and others, per the Homebrew executable list) run on a computer, and the docs mention capturing BLE traffic into Wireshark. I did not read the individual tool docs, so I can't say what each executable outputs.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a development platform for Bluetooth experimentation that ships with a capable BLE sniffer. The homepage describes it as an open source 2.4 GHz platform suitable for Bluetooth experimentation.
brief.how_it_works: The README and docs index I read do not explain the internal mechanism. The docs index lists pages on firmware, building from git, libbtbb (the companion library paired with each release), and Wireshark/PCAP capture, but I did not open them, so I can't describe the radio or decoding path beyond that.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, you need the physical Ubertooth One board, since the host tools talk to it. The README says firmware must be flashed (instructions are on the readthedocs firmware page), and libbtbb must be built from its 2020-12-R1 release, which is paired with the 2020-12-R1 Ubertooth release. Build steps are on the readthedocs build_guide page, which I did not open. The docs index also lists a 'Building from git' page, which I did not read.
brief.standout: It is a cheap, open 2.4 GHz board that turns a desk into a BLE sniffing station with Wireshark output. Its Bluetooth Classic capture is partial, which the README states plainly.
brief.status: Quiet. The README names 2020-12-R1 as the latest release, and the docs release notes stop at 2018-12-R1. The homepage says the Ubertooth One hardware is retired and that Great Scott Gadgets has no plan to manufacture more. I could not see commit dates, so I can't confirm recent development.
brief.caveats: The hardware is retired and no new units are planned, so you'll need a used board. Classic Bluetooth support is only partial (sniffing 'some data'). The README says there are no support staff on duty at all times, and GitHub 'technical support' issues get a response time of about two weeks. Most setup depends on building and flashing from separate docs pages that I did not read.
quotes: Project Ubertooth is an open source wireless development platform suitable for Bluetooth experimentation.
Ubertooth ships with a capable BLE (Bluetooth Smart) sniffer and can sniff some data from Basic Rate (BR) Bluetooth Classic connections.
Note: Ubertooth One is a retired product at this time. Great Scott Gadgets does not currently have a plan to manufacture more.
